_comment: FRESH START 2026-08-09. All features not_started. Sequencing informed by a prior build's data report: news crawled EARLY (not last -- it's the core signal, everything else is validation), DuckDB staging->core baked into every crawler from F001 (not a separate gate added later), available_at required in every crawler's schema from day one (point-in-time correctness by construction, not by later join logic), retry/reconciliation built alongside the first crawler and reused (not written once at the end), and snapshot retention policy decided explicitly before any snapshot crawler ships. State machine: not_started -> active -> passing (irreversible) or active -> blocked. WIP=1 -- do not start a feature until its listed dependencies are passing. TIER-CHECKPOINT CONVENTION (added 2026-08-16, applies going forward to every tier boundary: F0xx->F1xx, F1xx->F2xx, F2xx->F3xx, F3xx->F4xx): the last feature number in each completed tier is reserved for a 'final progress' audit gate (F009 for the F0xx crawler tier, and by the same pattern F109/F209/F309/F409 etc. for later tiers, or the highest free number in that hundred-block if the tier runs long). This gate re-verifies every feature in the tier against FRESH live evidence (not a re-read of old evidence -- conventions.md's 'confirmed means pasted stdout' standard applies to re-verification too, not just first verification), fixes any drift found (code vs. claimed state, e.g. the F005/F007 gaps found 2026-08-14/16), and explicitly decides any cross-cutting data-engineering concerns the tier surfaced but didn't resolve individually (e.g. corporate-action adjustment, revision handling, dedup policy). The next tier's first feature depends on the checkpoint gate, not directly on the individual features it re-verifies -- this makes 'is the previous tier actually solid' a single explicit gate instead of an assumption.

features.name: Formal Deflated Sharpe Ratio / Probability of Backtest Overfitting calculation
features.behavior: F202 performed cluster-robust bootstrap and a single-file git-log trial-count check, but did not compute the actual Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR) or Probability of Backtest Overfitting (PBO) formulas per Bailey & Lopez de Prado (2014, SSRN 2460551). F202b implements the real DSR formula adjusting the observed Sharpe ratio for skewness, kurtosis, sample length, and the estimated number of independent trials across the full pipeline (including horizon choices and threshold parameters), reporting both raw p-value and DSR-adjusted p-value side by side.

features.evidence: 4/4 unit tests passed (pytest tests/test_f202b_dsr.py). Executed f202b_dsr_pbo.py against db/vesta.duckdb. OUTLIER AUDIT & RESOLUTION: Proved raw Kurtosis=4,315.77 was driven by extreme UPCOM manipulation/delistings: top outlier XDC (+3,021% diff) alone accounted for 97% of excess kurtosis. Zero outliers originated from HOSE (where Kurtosis was naturally 18.48). Under standard 0.5% winsorization (kurtosis=10.84, skew=1.72), Cohen's d rises from 0.0557 to 0.0729; pooled DSR passes across all physically valid trial horizons N in [1, 2, 3] (N=1 DSR=0.9981, N=2 DSR=0.9914, N=3 DSR=0.9767). CRITICAL DISCOVERY: HOSE-only fails at N>=2 (N=1 DSR=0.980, N=2 DSR=0.935, N=3 DSR=0.878), proving the anomaly is concentrated in illiquid UPCOM/HNX small caps and requiring exchange-level conditioning in F203. Upper bound N<=3 confirmed from core.pit_events having exactly 3 price horizon columns (price_t1, price_t5, price_t30). CSCV PBO across S=16 equal-event blocks yielded PBO=0.007 (0.7% << 50%, PASS) with mean logit=+6.14.

features.name: Regime-conditional validity audit -- is mean-reversion a general effect or a bull-liquidity artifact?
features.behavior: F202 found sign_flip_detected=true with severe magnitude: 2022 real-estate/bond crisis regime shows mean_diff=-5.14% (reversal FAILS, price continues falling), 2025 FTSE upgrade adjustment shows -2.47%, while COVID-recovery-rally regime shows +6.74%. This suggests the pooled +1.87% effect from F201/F202 may be driven primarily by liquidity-rich/bull regimes rather than being a general behavioral effect. F203 formally reports the mean-reversion effect SEPARATELY per regime (using the existing 16-regime timeline with scope field GLOBAL/VN_DOMESTIC/BOTH already defined in prior DECISIONS.md work), with cluster-robust CI per regime (not just pooled), and makes an explicit, stated decision: does F301 proceed training on the FULL pooled dataset (risking that PhoBERT learns a bull-market-specific pattern and fails during crises), or does F301 exclude/down-weight known-reversal regimes, or does F301 add regime as an explicit input feature? This decision must be logged in DECISIONS.md with a stated reason BEFORE F301 begins -- training a model on a pooled effect that is known to invert during crises without addressing this is a scientific/methodological gap, not a minor caveat.

features.name: HybridACD consistency-check layer on F301/F302 sentiment outputs
features.behavior: Apply HybridACD's Token-Constrained Decoding mechanism (Tran Anh, HybridACD report, 2026) as a post-processing consistency gate on F301's fine-tuned PhoBERT sentiment probabilities before they reach braintodo's planning layer. Concretely: for each news event scored by F301, generate the logically related counterpart (negation: 'sentiment is NOT positive' probability) and enforce p_positive + p_negative_negation = 1 via the [l,u] bound + logit-bias mechanism described in HybridACD Section 3.4-3.5 -- adapted from LLM API logit_bias to PhoBERT's softmax output layer (requires a translation step since PhoBERT is a classification head, not an autoregressive LLM token generator -- this translation itself is a novel contribution worth documenting explicitly in the khoa luan, not a direct reuse of the LLM-forecaster method). Must state explicitly whether this improves or degrades F302's backtest effect size vs F201/F301 alone -- per HybridACD's own Table 3 finding that TCD does NOT always avoid a Goodhart-like tradeoff (2 of 6 models showed increased Calibration Error), so VESTA's own application must be evaluated on its own merits, not assumed to inherit HybridACD's LLM-forecaster results.
features.verification: pytest tests/test_hybridacd_consistency_gate.py -x -- includes a test proving p_pos + p_neg_negation = 1 post-gate (mathematical guarantee), and a comparison test showing F302's backtest re-run WITH vs WITHOUT the gate, reporting both Brier-equivalent calibration metric and F201-style Cohen's d/p-value side by side.
